references.disposition: The membership statement (s,t)∈R is precisely the defining interpretation of a binary relation represented as subset R⊆S×T. Cartesian product and subset meanings are linked; there is no required single-valuedness, totality or separately definable predicate introduced by this notation.
A relation may associate zero, one or many outputs to same input; unlike total function.

references.disposition: Properness m⊊R together with the no-intermediate-ideal condition (every ideal J with m⊆J⊆R equals m or R) is exactly the defining maximality predicate of the ideal m in the source. The ring, ideal and inclusion/proper-subset notions are already addressed (including the earlier amendment of the ambient ring). It is not an independently missing maximal-ideal meaning or a prime-ideal condition.
This is maximal among proper ideals; it is not the same predicate as being prime in a general ring.
